_comment: The synthetic half of the demo data, kept apart from anything measured and
keyed by the page it belongs to. Everything build_demo_data.py derives from
a real bundle (CPU, clients, channel counts, neighbour rows, the roaming
client) stays real and only has its identifiers replaced. These entries are
invented, because a bench with one DUT attached cannot produce a fleet, the
reference capture contained no crash lines, and connection state is live UI
that no capture records. Each page prints which of its content is synthetic.
MACs use the 02: locally-administered prefix so they are visibly not real.

files.html and bulletin.html are synthetic in full. A workspace file list and a note board are CONTENT, not measurements, so there is no measured claim to preserve. Names here are deliberate placeholders (Doe/Roe/Coe) and the note bodies are generic: an earlier revision reused real colleagues' names straight from the bench database, which is exactly what 'synthetic' was meant to prevent. Both pages say so in their provenance line.

serial-console.html: the Monitor half is real log lines chosen by the identifier guard. The vi session under Terminal is a scripted recording -- the product runs xterm.js over a pty on /ws/term, which a single offline file cannot be, so the page replays and says so rather than pretending. The config shown is invented; its ssid is a DemoAP-* placeholder like everywhere else.

firmware.html is synthetic: image names, checksums and the DUT address are invented. The transport contract is NOT — api takes the encrypted image, gui takes the signed .sig, and they are not interchangeable (firmware_service.py). A demo of a flasher that blurred that would be teaching the one mistake that cost this project two sessions.

posts.title: Lab unit booked for a long capture until Friday
posts.author: Alex Doe
posts.body: Running a 40-hour telemetry capture for the offline-analysis acceptance. Please leave the serial adapter alone — the console needs a human login after any reboot and a reconnect would end the run.

comments.author: Sam Roe
comments.body: Noted — I'll use the spare unit for the 6 GHz checks.

replies.author: Alex Doe
replies.body: Good, that one has the newer telemetry script with the per-radio client markers.

comments.author: Jo Coe
comments.body: Bundle looked right on my side: two CSVs, nine plots, no empty files.

posts.title: 2.4 GHz is saturated in this room
posts.author: Sam Roe
posts.body: Latest survey has 2.4 GHz utilisation at 85-94% all day, with over a thousand neighbouring SSIDs across the band. The recommendation moves us off the busiest channel. 5 GHz is fine.

comments.author: Alex Doe
comments.body: Matches the offline render. Worth moving before the next long run.

posts.title: Firmware upgrade went through cleanly
posts.author: Jo Coe
posts.body: Upload took about 24 s, the downloader ran, and the unit came back healthy. The device logged the reboot as a local-UI firmware upgrade.
